According to Bloomberg, OpenAI's first product to enter the hardware market is expected to be a portable, screenless smart speaker. Details are as follows.

One of five products in development

Although OpenAI announced its entry into the hardware market as early as May 2025, together with Jony Ive's io Products, the project has since gone quiet, until Apple filed a trade secrets lawsuit, which once again drew outside attention to the products OpenAI is developing.

Shortly after the initial announcement, another company, iyO, filed a trademark infringement lawsuit against OpenAI and io Products, and the related court documents revealed for the first time what the project is "not": the first device under development is neither a wearable nor an in-ear product.

Now, Bloomberg has reported the true positioning of the device. The report reads as follows:

and

Popular comments posted by DHa

I don't find this product very appealing. I don't want to carry my phone, go through a whole setup process, and then drag a device roughly the size of a HomePod around with me.

The report points out that the device can be plugged in and left in a room for extended use, but at the same time has a built-in rechargeable battery, "allowing users to carry it with them as they move between different rooms throughout the day":

The report also mentions that, although it is inevitable for the outside world to compare it with Apple's HomePod—especially amid the intense attention on Apple's trade secrets lawsuit—"OpenAI believes its first product has not infringed on any trade secrets."

Finally, Bloomberg points out that this smart speaker is only one of approximately five products OpenAI is currently developing. The company's long-term plans are also reported to include "a mobile AI device that could replace a smartphone." At the same time, the company has "also explored wearable products, including pendant-style devices, and has expressed interest in home robotics technology."
